name: Handling Unpermitted Work When Adding an ADU in Los Angeles County

mainEntity.name: How do ADU additions contractors in Los Angeles County handle projects when the main house already has unpermitted work?
mainEntity.text: How do ADU additions contractors in Los Angeles County handle projects when the main house already has unpermitted work?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many homes in Los Angeles County contain some unpermitted modifications, and these often surface when planning an ADU addition. When your contractor submits plans, city reviewers compare the drawings to available records and may flag areas of your home that were never legally permitted or do not match existing permits. ADU additions contractors generally cannot ignore these discrepancies. Safety‑critical issues—such as unpermitted bedrooms, conversions, or structural changes—often must be addressed as part of the ADU project. That can mean documenting and legalizing the prior work with as‑built plans and inspections or, in some cases, partially demolishing and rebuilding to current standards. This can add cost and time, so an experienced contractor will ask early about any known unpermitted work and walk the property looking for clues like non‑matching electrical panels, improvised plumbing, or irregular additions. They may recommend a phased strategy, bundling legalization work with your ADU addition to minimize disruption. Before you proceed, ask your contractor how they have handled similar situations, what kinds of unpermitted work typically trigger required corrections, and whether they expect your project to reveal any of these issues. Planning for this upfront reduces surprises during plan check or final inspection.
acceptedAnswer.description: If your main house has unpermitted work, ADU additions contractors in Los Angeles County typically must disclose and correct any safety-critical issues during the ADU project. Cities may require that certain unpermitted additions or conversions be legalized or removed before final approval of the new ADU addition.
